extracted.intended_audience: general newspaper readers / the public (wartime readership)
extracted.subtask_description: News reporting and commentary about wartime events and the role of newspapers in informing and mobilizing the public; includes examples and normative statements about what newspapers should do during the war. Geared toward readers and civic actors interested in press contributions to the national effort.

rubrics_metrics.name: Report fairly and fully the deliberations of Congress
rubrics_metrics.description: “the press which, with a very few exceptions, has reported fairly and fully the deliberations of the Congress.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The page asserts as a standard that newspapers should report congressional deliberations fairly and fully so the public is correctly informed; this is cited as evidence of the press’s indispensable role.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distribute public information quickly and in proper detail
rubrics_metrics.description: “To distribute such information quickly to every city and farm, to set it out in proper detail,”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: News outlets should rapidly disseminate government communications and regulations across the country and present them with sufficient detail for public comprehension and use.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide practical forms and tools in columns to aid citizens
rubrics_metrics.description: “Newspapers stepped into the breach and printed forms in their own columns so that housewives could clip them and use them when they visited their rationing boards.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A concrete expectation: newspapers may publish usable materials (forms, instructions) to help citizens comply with wartime administrative processes—an example of practical public service journalism.

rubrics_metrics.name: Focus public attention to support production and mobilization
rubrics_metrics.description: “present the problem to the American people and have labored steadily to help government and suppliers set up an efficient program of production.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Journalism should spotlight national production and mobilization needs, helping to coordinate public support and industrial response during wartime.

rubrics_metrics.name: Attribute reporting to official sources and bulletins
rubrics_metrics.description: Frequent use of attributions such as “By the Associated Press,” “a Government bulletin announced,” and named spokesmen in reports.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The article models and implies a standard that wartime reports should clearly cite official sources, spokesmen, and wire services to establish credibility and provenance of information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include concrete figures and specific operational details
rubrics_metrics.description: The dispatch supplies counts and measurements (e.g., numbers of ships sunk, production totals like “5,500 planes” or “70,000 aircraft bombs of 1,000 pounds or larger”).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reports are expected to provide quantitative specifics—casualty counts, production numbers, locations, unit names—so readers grasp scale and concrete impact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treat the press as an essential contributor to the war effort
rubrics_metrics.description: Statements such as “With the nation at war ... it is a contribution which should clearly indicate that the press must ... contribute to the war effort.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Normative stance: newspapers are not merely observers but play an active, necessary role (information, morale, organization) and should be recognized/protected in that role.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publish names and particulars of servicemen, wounded, missing, and interned civilians
rubrics_metrics.description: The War Department’s lists of names and places of internment and the publication of casualty and wounded lists in the paper.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A responsibility of wartime reporting is to maintain public records of individuals affected by the war (names, ranks, relations, addresses) to inform families and communities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use on-the-ground dispatches and correspondents for frontline perspective
rubrics_metrics.description: Bylines and references to bureau chiefs and correspondents (e.g., Henry C. Cassidy, chief of the Associated Press bureau in Moscow) and reports from multiple fronts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Wartime journalism should rely on field correspondents and bureau reporting to convey firsthand observations, providing timeliness and authenticity to coverage.
